summary: Varnondor's capes and lanterns: the sea watch, harbours for the host, open, close or watch for Parim, the cape levy and the fleets that gather.

approach_watchers.name: Watchers of the Approaches
approach_watchers.desc: The capes of Varnondor face the wide central sea, and every headland has its lamp and its watchman. Not a hull has come within a day's sail unseen since the First Age.

peninsula_crown.name: The Peninsula Crown
peninsula_crown.desc: The king wears a crown of silvered iron, shaped like the lantern-tower on the great cape. Four states are held by it, and none has ever left it.

cape_lights.name: Lighthouses of the Capes
cape_lights.desc: Every headland has a tower with a fire on its crown, kept by a family who inherit the work. The lights can be seen from the open sea on a clear night.

far_shore_watch.name: Watch on the Far Shore
far_shore_watch.desc: Fast boats go out each dusk toward the Middle Lands, and come home each dawn. What they see is written down and given to the king.

muster_harbour.name: The Muster Harbour
muster_harbour.desc: The great harbour of the peninsula is arranged to take a whole fleet: a hundred berths, pitch-sheds, stores and cisterns. A host can embark from it in a week.

approaches_closed.name: The Approaches Closed
approaches_closed.desc: The king has barred the sea-lanes past his capes to every war-fleet. His forts are manned, his chains are drawn and his lanterns are dark.

kings_lanterns.name: The King's Lanterns
kings_lanterns.desc: The lamps of the peninsula now burn at Parim's bidding as well as the king's own. Their light shows an Aenoran ship the safe way into harbour.

cape_sea_soldiers.name: Sea Soldiers of the Capes
cape_sea_soldiers.desc: The cape-wardens are trained to leap from a boat onto a beach with a shield on the arm and a spear in the hand. They are a small band, and a very rough one.

first_ashore_host.name: First Ashore
first_ashore_host.desc: The cape-wardens are the first men over the side of the first boats. They carry a strip of cloth in the colours of Varnondor, and they plant it on the sand.

lanterns_on_the_capes.title: Lanterns on the Capes
lanterns_on_the_capes.desc: A fast boat from Varnondor has anchored under the sea-wall at Parim. The king of the capes, it says, would light his lanterns for Aenor's ships, for a price and a promise: that the crown remember the cape lords, who have watched the central sea for a thousand years.

focuses.name: King Oslin's Court
focuses.desc: Varnondor is a small kingdom of four states on an eastern peninsula, facing the wide central sea. King Oslin keeps lighthouses burning on every headland, and sleeps beside a window.

focuses.name: The Cape Lords
focuses.desc: The lords of the capes hold their heads high and their towers higher. They meet at the king's table each quarter, and the talk is always of weather.

focuses.name: The King's Harbour
focuses.desc: The king's own harbour is dredged and a new mole is built. It is the nearest western anchorage to the Middle Lands, and the king knows how much that is worth.

focuses.name: The Old Landings Remembered
focuses.desc: Stone markers are set on the beaches where Aenor's fleets once came ashore. The cape lords read the names aloud at the autumn feast.

effects.tooltip: Aenor's fleets came ashore on these capes in the First Age.

focuses.name: The Peninsula Crown
focuses.desc: A crown of silvered iron, in the shape of a lantern-tower, is made for King Oslin. He wears it to the lighting of the first lamp each dusk.

focuses.name: The Blue-Sea Approaches
focuses.desc: The sea-lanes past Varnondor's capes are the approaches to the Middle Lands. The king plants a fort at each narrows, with a chain and a lantern.

focuses.name: Lighthouses of the Capes
focuses.desc: Tall towers go up on the headlands, each a little higher than the last. Their keepers are paid by the king and fed by the villagers.

focuses.name: Cape Forts
focuses.desc: Old forts on the capes are rebuilt in stone, with sea-gates and catapult platforms. Each has a garrison and a well, and all of them look out to sea.

focuses.name: The Sea Watch
focuses.desc: Lady Sevra of the Capes commands the sea watch from the great light-tower. She has sharper eyes than any of her wardens, and a very short temper.

focuses.name: Watch on the Far Shore
focuses.desc: Fast boats are sent across the central sea to watch the Middle Lands' coast. They carry no cargo, only a lamp, a pair of keen eyes and a promise to return.

focuses.name: Harbours of the Peninsula
focuses.desc: The peninsula's coves are dredged and their quays rebuilt. A fleet that anchors there will find fresh water, dry stores and a wayfinder at the gate.

focuses.name: The Staging Yards
focuses.desc: Slips and pitch-sheds are built to refit and repair a fleet in a week. The western fleet may use them, if the Ford Council asks nicely.

focuses.name: Anchorages of the Peninsula
focuses.desc: Deep-water anchorages are marked with buoys and moorings, and a harbour-master is stationed at each. A hundred ships can lie in them in a gale.

focuses.name: The Muster Harbour
focuses.desc: The greatest harbour of the peninsula is arranged to take a whole fleet at once: berths, stores, cisterns, pitch and a long beach for embarking troops. A host can sail from it in a week.

focuses.name: Wayfinders of the Approaches
focuses.desc: The best sailors of the capes are taught the safe channels past every reef. They guide any fleet that asks, and learn what the fleets are doing as they go.

focuses.name: The Old Grudge
focuses.desc: Varnondor's grudge is the grudge of a watchman, who remembers where the enemy came ashore. The king puts the question to his lords: what do the capes owe to Aenor?

focuses.name: Close the Approaches
focuses.desc: The king orders his chains drawn across every narrows and his lanterns put out. No war-fleet shall pass the capes, whatever flag it flies.

focuses.name: Open the Approaches
focuses.desc: The king opens his harbours to the western fleet, and lights his lanterns for its ships. The old watchmen mutter, but the young ones are glad.

focuses.name: Lanterns for Parim
focuses.desc: The king sends word to Parim that his lanterns burn for the crown. It is an old watchman's trick: to light the lamp for the strongest, and wait to see who comes.

focuses.name: The Neutral Capes
focuses.desc: The capes are neutral, and the king says so on every wall. His lords are not asked to pick a side, and his ports are not asked to take a flag.

focuses.name: A Delegate from the Capes
focuses.desc: A cape lord is sent to sit at the Ford Council. He brings his own chair, a chart of the approaches and a firm opinion about where the fleet should anchor.

focuses.name: The King's Lanterns
focuses.desc: The capes now burn their lamps at the bidding of the crown. A royal galley is welcome in every harbour, and no ship is stopped without leave.

focuses.name: The Varnondor Pledge
focuses.desc: The cape lords stand at the lamp-tower and pledge their hosts to the Crossing, one by one. The king is the last to speak, and says only: we know the sea.

focuses.name: The Cape Levy
focuses.desc: Every village of the capes provides a man for the king's host. They are fishers and lamp-keepers, and they can all swim.

focuses.name: Sea Soldiers of the Capes
focuses.desc: Cape-Warden Tomas Reed is given the task of teaching the levy to fight from boats and to storm a beach. He teaches by example, and bruises easily.

focuses.name: Bows of the Capes
focuses.desc: The cape bowmen shoot from the walls of the forts and from the decks of the boats. Their bows are short, their arrows are long and their aim is excellent.

focuses.name: The Peninsula Host
focuses.desc: The levy, the sea soldiers and the bowmen are joined in a single host. It marches under the lantern banner, and keeps time with the drum.

focuses.name: The Fleets Gather
focuses.desc: The ships of the West have begun to assemble in the harbours of the peninsula. The king stands on the great cape and watches them come in, hull after hull, to the lighting of the lamps.

focuses.name: First Ashore
focuses.desc: The cape-wardens go in the first boats, with a flag of Varnondor on a staff. They are the first to land, and the first to dig in.

focuses.name: The Capes Hold
focuses.desc: The king keeps his hosts at home, and his lanterns burning. Whatever the fleets do on the far shore, the capes will be there when they come back.

focuses.name: Stranded on the Far Shore
focuses.desc: Some of the first ashore did not sail home. They hold a beach on the far coast, and they have a new banner to rally to.

focuses.name: The Capes Remember
focuses.desc: The ships come home to the capes, or they do not. The king lights the lamps for all of them, and keeps the great lamp burning until dawn.
